page: Microsoft Azure FX48mds belongs to the compute-optimized FX family and features a memory-intensive architecture paired with dedicated Intel x86_64 processors. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 48 dedicated virtual CPUs and 1008.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 21.0 GB per vCPU. Accelerated hardware vector instructions and cryptographic hardware extensions are absent in the instance metadata configuration.

Storage configuration includes 2165 GB of local solid-state disk (SSD) storage, and the instance supports Premium Storage. The server does not feature discrete GPU accelerators and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring auxiliary networking allocation for public internet connectivity.

Resource allocation focuses on high memory density per compute thread alongside fast local scratch disk capacity. Qualitative cost efficiency stems from consolidating workloads that demand substantial memory footprints per core without requiring GPU acceleration. The combination of dedicated compute and massive RAM capacity targets enterprise in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, and memory-bound batch analytics.
description: Microsoft Azure FX48mds is a high-memory compute instance driven by dedicated Intel x86_64 processor cores on the Microsoft Hyper-V platform. It integrates 48 dedicated vCPUs with 1008.0 GB of system memory, delivering 21.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server features 2165 GB of local SSD scratch storage and supports Azure Premium Storage, operating without discrete GPU accelerators. Because the virtual core allocation provides an unusually dense memory ratio alongside local solid-state disk capacity, the hardware footprint is tailored for resource-intensive processes that encounter RAM bottlenecks on conventional compute nodes. The FX48mds is built for large-scale in-memory database deployments, electronic design automation pipelines, complex mathematical modeling, and demanding batch analytical processing.
